As far as I know, the name Yeshua means The LORD's Salvation, or Cry Out to the LORD for Help.

It is the shortened version of Yehoshua, literally "YHWH saves (or turns) us".

Prior to being transliterated from the Hebrew Bible, the name Ἰησοῦς (Iesous) did not exist in Greek. Through multiple translations and changes in pronunciation, a tradition of saying "Jesus" has obscured His name, "Yeshua."

If we had forgotten the name of our God, Or extended our hands to a strange god; 21Would not God find this out?

For He knows the secrets of the heart.

Psalm 44:20-21

The first letter in the name Yeshua ("Jesus") is the yod and it represents the "Y" sound in Hebrew. Many names in the Bible that begin with yod are transliterated in the English Bibles with the letter "J" rather than "Y".

In early English the letter "J" was pronounced the way we pronounce "Y" today as in yellow.

Because English pronunciation has shifted to what we know today, these transliterations were not altered.

Thus, such Hebrew place names as ye-ru-sha-LA-yim, ye-ri-HO, and yar-DEN have become known to us as Jerusalem, Jericho, and Jordan; and Hebrew personal names such as yo-NA, yi-SHAI, and ye-SHU-a have become known to us as Jonah, Jesse, and Jesus.
